Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 77:

﴿O you who have believed, bow and prostrate⟩ in your prayer. He commanded them to do both because they had not been performing them at the beginning of Islam. Or, they prayed, and he expressed the prayer by these two, because they are the greatest of its pillars (arkan). Or, submit to Allah and fall down before Him in prostration. ﴿And worship your Lord⟩ with all the acts of worship He has prescribed for you. ﴿And do good⟩ and seek out what is better and more righteous in what you do and what you leave undone, such as the voluntary acts of obedience (nawafil al-ta'at), maintaining ties of kinship (silat al-arham), and noble moral conduct (makarim al-akhlaq). ﴿That you may succeed⟩ meaning: do all of these while hoping for success, not certain of it, and not relying confidently on your own deeds. The verse is, according to us, a verse of prostration (ayat sajdah), because of the command to prostrate in it, and because of his saying, upon him be prayer and peace: "Surat al-Hajj was favoured with two prostrations; whoever does not prostrate for them, let him not recite it."

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 78:

﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him﴾. That is, for the sake of Allah and for His sake, against the enemies of His religion, both the outward ones such as the people of deviation, and the inward ones such as desire (hawa) and the self (nafs).

And it is related from him, upon him be blessings and peace, that when he returned from the expedition of Tabuk he said: "We have returned from the lesser jihad (al-jihad al-asghar) to the greater jihad (al-jihad al-akbar)."

﴿with the striving due to Him﴾: that is, striving in which there is sincere truth, purely for His sake. The word "truth" (haqq) is placed before "striving" (jihad) as an intensification, just as you say: "He is the truth of a scholar" (huwa haqqu 'alim). The word "striving" is attributed to the pronoun (i.e., "His striving") either for breadth of usage, or because it is specific to Allah in that it is done for the sake of the countenance of Allah, the Exalted, and for His sake.

﴿He has chosen you﴾: He has selected you for His religion and for supporting it. In this there is an alert to the requirement of jihad and to the one who calls to it. And in His saying: ﴿and He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾: that is, narrowness, by imposing what would be hard to carry out upon you. This indicates that there is no obstacle for them in it and no excuse for them in abandoning it, or it indicates a concession regarding neglecting some of what He commanded them, where it would be difficult for them, based on his saying, upon him be blessings and peace: "When I command you with something, then carry out from it what you are able."

It has also been said that this means He made for them a way out of every sin, by granting them concessions in tight situations and opening for them the door of repentance, and by prescribing for them expiations (kaffarat) for the rights of Allah and compensations (arsh) and blood-money (diyat) for the rights of the servants.

﴿the religion of your father Abraham﴾: it is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar), governed by a verb implied by the meaning of what precedes it, with the genitive construction omitted; that is, "He has widened your religion with the widening of the religion of your father." Or it is in the accusative by way of incitement (al-igra') or of specification (al-ikhtisas). He made him their father because he is the father of the Messenger of Allah, upon him be blessings, and he is like a father to his community in that he is the cause of their everlasting life and of their existence in the manner that is valued in the Hereafter. Or because most of the Arabs were from his offspring, so they were given precedence over others.

﴿It is He who named you Muslims before﴾: before the Qur'an, in the earlier scriptures.

﴿and in this﴾: and in the Qur'an. The pronoun refers to Allah, the Exalted, and this is supported by the reading "Allah has named you" (Allahu sammakum). Or it refers to Ibrahim, and their being named Muslims in the Qur'an, even though it is not from it, was on account of his naming them before, in His saying: ﴿and of our offspring a Muslim community for You﴾. It has also been said that its estimated meaning is "and in this is the explanation of His naming you Muslims."

﴿so that the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ on the Day of Resurrection: the phrase is connected to "named you." ﴿a witness over you﴾: that he conveyed to you; this indicates the acceptance of his testimony for himself, relying on his infallibility, or by obedience to whoever obeys and disobedience to whoever disobeys.

﴿and that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ by conveying the messengers to them. ﴿So establish prayer and give zakat﴾: draw near to Allah, the Exalted, with all kinds of acts of obedience, for having singled you out with this grace and honor. ﴿And hold fast to Allah﴾: trust in Him in all your affairs, and do not seek help or support except from Him. ﴿He is your Protector﴾: your helper and the one who manages your affairs. ﴿How excellent is the Protector and how excellent is the Helper﴾: for He, glorified is He, has no equal in guardianship and support, rather in reality there is no protector and no helper other than Him.

From the Prophet, upon him be blessings and peace: "Whoever recites Surat al-Hajj will be given a reward like one Hajj he performed and one 'Umrah he performed, equal to the number of those who performed Hajj and 'Umrah in the past and in the future."
